conclusions: Only board psram_dma_direct flag changes; 40 MHz, 4092-byte chunks, queue depth 2 and existing completion ownership remain.
Real IDF allocation, heap alignment, LCD queue and release functions reproduce baseline internal-copy failure and successful external TX under internal pressure.
Source inventory, effective configuration, protected artifacts, candidate App and ELF were independently checked; internal static data remain 65216 bytes.
App transaction checks current identity and paired resources; failures restore the same-run App; recovery preserves runtime NVS and is independent of older candidates.
Documentation correctly distinguishes completed offline work from pending device installation and physical display acceptance.
limits: Host model checks byte contents and queued-buffer lifetime; it does not emulate actual ISR scheduling, memory-bus contention or display output.
Alignment sanitizer alone is disabled to model S3 byte-addressable EDMA with original uint32_t pointer signatures; C assertions and other checks remain.
Monitor DMA TX underflow and NO_MEM during device validation. Physical acceptance is pending reconnection of the identified head.
